title: Cap. VI Arg. 11: Matt. 24 — for the elect days shortened; God removes every obstacle
pass_a_gloss: Hither look those sayings of Christ the Savior, Matt. 24: So that into error may be led, if it were possible, even the elect. For the elect's sake those days shall be shortened. Such therefore is the decree of election, that by reason of it God takes upon himself to remove all obstacles which would impede the salvation of the elect, and to procure for them those means which will infallibly produce their salvation.
pass_b_english: So Christ's words in Matt. 24: to lead astray, if possible, even the elect — and for the elect's sake those days will be shortened. The election decree is of that kind: by it God takes on himself to remove every obstacle that would block the elect's salvation, and to procure means that will infallibly produce it.
source_text: Horsum spectant illa Christi Servatoris dicta, Matt. xxiv: Ita ut in errorem inducantur, si fieri posset, etiam electi. Propter electos breviabuntur dies illi. Tale est ergo decretum electionis, ut ratione illius Deus in se suscipiat omnes obices removere, quae salutem electorum impedirent, et iis ea media procurare, quae salutem eorundem infallibiliter producent.
